still_true: Wegovy's US list price is still $1,349 a month, and almost nobody pays it.
The FDA has approved no generic semaglutide or tirzepatide in the US; generic liraglutide is still the only generic incretin on the US market.
The TrumpRx cash channel still operates, and oral Wegovy starting doses still cost $149 a month there (maintenance still $199).
Medicare still pays for no incretin prescribed for weight loss alone: the Medicare GLP-1 Bridge pilot has not been revived and Congress has not reopened the ~$41B CBO-scored permanent benefit.

The September 2027 tri-agency guidance allowing up to 30% premium differentials tied to verified adherence still stands, Illinois's ban on adherence-conditioned premiums is still the only state ban in force, and the suicidal-ideation warning is still off the labels.

population.note: FICTIONAL. Cycling arithmetic: 43.0% ever-used − 31.6% current = 11.4% of adults who used and are off now. About 50% of current users are on a second or later course (15.8 points) and 3.2 points cycled and are off again, so (15.8 + 3.2) / 43.0 ≈ 44.2% of ever-users have cycled; the other 8.2 points stopped once and have not restarted. This fits persistence of about one-third at one year on cash oral and weekly products, ~60% in conditioned tracks, and restart rates of 36–47%. It also counts the newly common deliberate 'drug holiday': ~38% of current users report at least one holiday or self-reduction in the past year, but only stops longer than 8 weeks count as cycling here. Ever-use rose 8.4 points, mostly from three sources: 60+ starts on the tirzepatide dementia label (Jan 2036), state free-provision programmes, and the returning gray market. Age check: 0.20×17 + 0.33×30 + 0.23×44 + 0.24×34 = 3.4 + 9.9 + 10.12 + 8.16 ≈ 31.6. Income thirds average ≈ 31.7. Users: 31.6% of ~278M adults ≈ 87.8M. FICTIONAL payer mix: Medicare ~23.0M (26.2%, about 20.4M aged 65+ and 2.6M disabled under 65); Medicaid ~7.5M (8.5%: AUD label ~1.4M, dementia label for 60–64 and duals, plus the 7 states that cover weight loss); state free-provision programmes ~1.1M (1.3%); commercial ~17.5M (19.9%, of which ~10.6M are in conditioned tracks); legitimate cash ~29.7M (33.8%, including ~2.6M calm/focus subscribers and ~6.3M indefinite $149 starting-dose users); imported or counterfeit ~9.0M (10.3%). Sum: 23.0 + 7.5 + 1.1 + 17.5 + 29.7 + 9.0 = 87.8. Public payers together cover 31.6M (36%), more than any other channel, so for the first time public money is the default payer. 65+ check: 34% of ~66.7M ≈ 22.7M, of whom ~20.4M are Medicare-paid. Adult obesity ~31.3%. About 18% of adults have obesity and have never used a drug, still concentrated in the rural South outside the subsidy states, in Appalachia and among uninsured adults aged 50–64. Pediatric: 1.9% of under-18s, ~3.5% of 12–17s and ~0.65% of 6–11s; ~62% of 6–11 starts are Medicaid/CHIP. About 6.1M children live with a parent who has regained after stopping, and ~2.4M with a grandparent newly on the dementia label.

access.public_coverage: Medicare (~23.0M users) still pays nothing for weight loss alone. It now pays through diabetes, CV, CKD, OSA, AUD and, since Jan 2036, a dementia-risk label for adults 60+ with BMI ≥27 and no CVD requirement (tirzepatide). Because dementia risk reduction is not a weight-loss use, Part D plans must cover it behind PA, which requires a DXA or FRAX assessment. FICTIONAL arithmetic: 23.0M × ~$231 average net/month × 12 ≈ $63.8B gross Part D incretin spend (up from ~$38.3B). Dementia route: ~6.0M × $245 × 12 ≈ $17.6B. AUD route: ~1.1M × $205 × 12 ≈ $2.7B. Net prices did not fall, so all of the growth is volume. Medicaid (~7.5M): AUD and dementia uses are covered outpatient drugs everywhere under existing rebate law. 7 states still cover adult weight loss. Gross ≈ 7.5M × ~$190 × 12 ≈ $17.1B before statutory and supplemental rebates. State free provision (~1.1M) runs in 11 states: Mississippi, Alabama, Louisiana, Tennessee, Arkansas, Oklahoma, South Carolina and New Mexico cover obesity and AUD; Kentucky, West Virginia and Ohio cover AUD only. They buy the Wegovy pill from Novo at the TrumpRx prices of $149/$199, the purchases fall outside Medicaid best price as state pharmaceutical assistance programmes, and Novo declined to go lower. 1.1M × ~$152 × 12 ≈ $2.0B a year from general funds, tobacco money and opioid-settlement money.
access.generic_rest_of_world: Indian generic semaglutide is $4–30 a month inside India and in 100+ export markets, and Chinese tirzepatide-analogue vials are $20–60 where patents are not enforced. Canadian generic semaglutide is CAD 45–80 and Brazilian BRL 160–280. In Aug 2035 India suspended its direct-to-consumer export-licence checks after US–India trade talks collapsed. Since then, product transshipped through the UAE and Mexico reaches US addresses for ~$55–120, compared with $90–180 in 2034. India and China supply roughly 70% of world incretin volume.
access.note: FICTIONAL. Prices stalled. US branded net prices were flat in 2035 and 2036, ending the 3–5% annual drift. Three things drove it: Medicare dementia demand, an FDA shortage listing for oral amycretin (oral peptides need many times the API of injectables), and litigation reserves that both companies cite in pricing calls. TrumpRx: Wegovy pill $149 starting, $199 maintenance; Foundayo $149–229. Injectable Wegovy/Zepbound $249–299, MariTide $249 direct (~6.4M users), retatrutide ~$399. Oral amycretin is still ~$449 cash with no TrumpRx price, ~7.2M users, and is on the shortage list since Oct 2035. Orals are ~60% of users. Business Group on Health (Nov 2036): 34% of employers cover weight management, ~70% of them with adherence and progress conditions. Tracks hold ~10.6M. After the anhedonia label (Mar 2035), most tracks added a 'label-directed dose reduction' code so a clinician-documented dose cut does not count as non-adherence. Unlogged holidays still count. The Section 232 100% tariff stays in force. The gray market came back larger and dirtier: ~9.0M users, vials re-filled from smuggled API, and pressed counterfeit tablets sold as 'amycretin' into the shortage.

on_market_classes: GIP/GLP-1 dual agonist, weekly injectable (tirzepatide: Zepbound/Mounjaro)
GLP-1/amylin unimolecular co-agonist, daily oral (oral amycretin)
GLP-1 agonist/GIP-receptor antagonist antibody conjugate, monthly injectable (maridebart cafraglutide: MariTide)
GLP-1 agonist, daily oral peptide (Wegovy pill 25 mg; Rybelsus)
GLP-1 agonist, daily injectable (liraglutide: Saxenda, incl. generics)
Activin type II receptor antibody muscle adjunct (bimagrumab, restricted label)
indications_beyond_weight_and_diabetes: moderate-to-severe alcohol use disorder (oral semaglutide / Wegovy pill, Jan 2033; orforglipron / Foundayo, approved Jul 2036). VA/DoD guideline (Jun 2035) lists incretins as first-line alongside naltrexone and acamprosate
pediatric obesity ages 6–11 (liraglutide incl. generics; weekly semaglutide), with growth-velocity, Tanner and eating-disorder monitoring

reduction of risk of all-cause dementia: tirzepatide in adults with obesity and established CVD, extended in Jan 2036 to adults 60+ with BMI ≥27 regardless of CVD. The label requires a fracture-risk assessment and limits use in women 70+ with osteoporosis unless they are on antiresorptive therapy
mainstream_offlabel_uses: 'calm' and 'focus' low-dose plans (~2.6M subscribers, ~45% now written on an AUD label), rebranded after the anhedonia label as 'dose-tuned' plans with scheduled holidays
scheduled 'drug holidays' (weekends, weddings, funerals, holidays), often against label re-titration advice
dementia-prevention use by 50–59-year-olds below the label age, cash-paid
indefinite use of the $149 TrumpRx starting dose (~6.3M people)
semaglutide in 12–14-year-olds above label titration in gray channels
drugs.pipeline_note: FICTIONAL. Tirzepatide's 60+ dementia extension was resubmitted in Jan 2035 and approved in Jan 2036 (12 months), carrying the hip-fracture limitation from the confirmatory trial. Foundayo for AUD was filed in Jun 2035 and approved in Jul 2036 (13 months). Oral parity is now a supply story. Oral amycretin (~21.5%) remains the only pill at tirzepatide's level, and Novo's oral API capacity cannot meet demand: FDA shortage listing Oct 2035, allocation to existing patients first. No oral matches retatrutide's ~24%. Implants remain in phase 1–2 and are not on the US market. Bimagrumab's label was not widened, but users rose to ~0.4M as dementia-label DXA screening found high-risk patients. Global incretin market ~$235B (2035). US branded net prices were flat for two years.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Still the leading cause of discontinuation outside tracks. New: re-titration vomiting in people who restart at full dose after holidays (see rebound entry).

safety_ledger.effect: Gastroparesis, ileus and bowel obstruction (persistent delayed gastric emptying)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Persistence after stopping remains disputed. Of the first two MDL gastroparesis bellwethers, one ended in a defence verdict on causation (Jun 2035) and one in a $28M plaintiff verdict against Novo (Nov 2035). GI claims are ~46,000.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: No new labelling; more bellwethers set for 2037.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Elevated with rapid weight loss; unchanged.
No causal confirmation; absolute risk low; still pleaded with EPI.

safety_ledger.effect: Lean mass (muscle) loss and bone-density loss
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Medicare hip-fracture HR ~1.3 after more than 2 years and ~1.45 after three or more cycles. The excess in women 70+ on the dementia trial is now in the label. Early 2036 Part D claims show a rise in DXA orders, not yet in fractures.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Class warning; FRAX/DXA required by the dementia PA; bimagrumab for high-risk users.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Conflicting cohorts; absolute risk very low.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Listed in adverse reactions; no class warning.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: No adult signal, including in AUD-label and anhedonia-labelled cohorts.

safety_ledger.effect: Reward blunting / emotional flattening ('Ozempic personality', anhedonia)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: The class label (Mar 2035) gives the estimate: clinically meaningful anhedonia in ~6–8% of maintenance-dose users vs ~3–4% of comparators, ~10% on retatrutide, and ~5% at starting doses in Novo's required dose-stratified analysis. It usually eases within 4–8 weeks of a dose reduction. Nobody has measured how it interacts with the cognitive effects in 60+ dementia-label users.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: 505(o)(4) safety labelling change across the class, with a 'consider dose reduction' instruction and a medication-guide question set. FTC and FDA warned three calm platforms whose ads still said 'quiet the noise' without the risk.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Half to two-thirds regain within 18 months, worse after repeated cycles. The 2033 'tariff stoppers' have largely regained, and many restarted through subsidy programmes or the returning gray market.
B12, iron, vitamin D, and thiamine in AUD users who drink. Malnutrition flags in frail 75+ dementia-label users.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Annual panel language; thiamine counselling; geriatric nutrition screening added to the dementia PA.

safety_ledger.effect: Exocrine pancreatic insufficiency after 5+ years of continuous use
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: ~2× incidence after 5+ years of semaglutide; tirzepatide HR ~1.3. EPI claims ~58,000. Novo raised its reserve to ~$8.1B and is in global settlement talks. The DOJ civil investigation is open.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: EPI wording on semaglutide and tirzepatide labels; Form 483 closed out in 2035 after Novo's corrective plan.

safety_ledger.effect: Long-horizon effects beyond ~5 years; effects in children on drug for decades; effects of repeated on/off cycling
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: About fourteen years of semaglutide follow-up now. Holidays, cycling and indefinite starting-dose use are all still unstudied, and a 70-year-old starting a drug meant to run for decades is a new population.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Pediatric bone and growth PMRs continue; a dementia-label PMR covers fracture and frailty.

safety_ledger.effect: Compounded / counterfeit / imported product harms (dosing errors, contamination, substitution)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Adverse-event reports tied to non-approved product passed ~44,000. In Mar 2036, FDA and CDC tied pressed counterfeit 'oral amycretin' tablets, some containing sibutramine and bisacodyl and none any amycretin, to ~140 ED visits, 23 cardiac events and 6 deaths in 9 states. Re-filled vials caused another Burkholderia cluster in Alabama (~80 cases). Poison-centre calls are ~6× 2025 levels.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Import alert and public warning; CBP seizures up but small against mail volume. State subsidy programmes cite counterfeit harm as their rationale. No federal statute changed.

safety_ledger.effect: Growth deceleration, delayed puberty and restrictive eating in children started young
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Height-velocity deficits of ~0.5–0.6 cm/year persist in prepubertal starters, with partial catch-up after stopping. Swedish ARFID HR ~1.8. Final adult height unknown.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Monitoring language and medication guide; no REMS; AAP lifestyle-first for prepubertal children.

safety_ledger.effect: Alcohol-related harms on the AUD label (dehydration, alcoholic ketoacidosis, aspiration with vomiting during binge drinking)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: ~1 per 2,000 person-years, holding steady as the AUD population grew to ~3.6M across payers.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Counselling language carried onto the Foundayo AUD label; PMR ongoing.

safety_ledger.effect: Rebound and re-titration harms around drug holidays (vomiting, dehydration, binge eating or drinking during the off-days)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: ED networks report a Monday cluster of vomiting and dehydration in users who skip weekend doses and restart at full dose, plus binge-drinking episodes in AUD users on holidays. Rates are not yet estimated.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labels already say to re-titrate after missed doses; FDA added a holiday Q&A to medication guides (2036). No study required yet.

food_and_beverage.state: About 47% of households now have a user. Snack and confectionery volumes are down ~15–16% from 2025 and sugary drinks ~13%, and dollar sales fell again. The 2033 'tariff bounce' in lower-income zips reversed once subsidy programmes and cheap gray product returned. New: senior-oriented SKUs (soft protein, fortified small portions) for the 60+ dementia-label cohort, sold in Florida and Arizona retirement markets.

alcohol.state: US spirits volumes are down ~21% from 2025 and beer ~13%. The VA/DoD first-line guideline, Foundayo's AUD label and free AUD provision in Kentucky, West Virginia and Ohio reach heavy drinkers in exactly the industry's volume core. Kentucky bourbon cut another ~1,100 jobs, and two Bardstown-area craft distilleries closed. Holiday weekends now show small on-premise spikes, which bartenders call 'skip-day trade'.

restaurants.state: Traffic is flat to slightly down. Buffet and early-dinner chains in The Villages, Sun City and Myrtle Beach lose senior covers after the dementia label. Bars in Dayton and Toledo keep pill nights. QSR value traffic in Memphis softened again as Tennessee's programme enrolled users.

apparel.state: Plus-size keeps shrinking. Mature-market womenswear in Florida reports a size-down wave among 65+. Resale serves cyclers and holiday-takers.

fitness.state: Strength training keeps growing. Medicare Advantage plans bundle resistance classes with dementia-label PA to manage fracture risk, which suits SilverSneakers-type programmes and budget chains.

insurance.state: Part D is the story. Gross incretin spend is ~$63.8B, plan bids rose, and the 2036 and 2037 base premiums rose again. MA plans write their own fracture and nutrition protocols. Employer pharmacy trend is ~+6%, and tracks hold 10.6M. Medicaid budgets absorb AUD and dementia users without any state having chosen it. Eleven states now budget about $2B a year for direct provision.

pharma.state: Revenue still grows on volume. Prices are flat, Lilly is the largest beneficiary of the dementia label, and Novo is capacity-constrained on oral amycretin and carrying an ~$8.1B litigation reserve. Indian exporters regained US direct-to-consumer volume after India suspended its checks. Counterfeit tablet presses, mostly offshore, are now a distinct supply chain.

body_and_culture.what_the_body_signals: Age has joined class as a reading. A thinner 70-year-old in The Villages signals 'brain pill' and a Part D plan, not vanity. Lifted and scanned still means covered and coached. Slow-thin on the $149 starting dose means cash. In Mississippi a county-health pill bottle with a state seal has become ordinary, and in some congregations it is a mark against you.
body_and_culture.thinness_and_class: Muscle stays the upper-tier uniform. 'Off-drug lean' is still the Austin and Charlotte boast, and now 'never needed a holiday' joins it. The bottom third's use rose fastest, through state programmes and the cheap gray market, so the 2034 regain gap in the Delta has narrowed. It narrowed partly on counterfeit product.
body_and_culture.eating_as_ritual: Holiday dinners now come with announced dose skips. Families in Ohio and Kentucky talk about 'skipping for Thanksgiving' the way earlier generations talked about loosening a belt. Bread Alone (~1,300 congregations) runs 'full table' suppers that ask guests to come off for the day. Retirement communities replace dessert carts with protein courses.
body_and_culture.dating_and_intimacy: Profiles now carry 'dose-tuned' and 'on holiday' as well as 'calm plan' and 'on AUD treatment'. Many daters read the anhedonia label as permission to ask about a partner's dose directly.
body_and_culture.meaning_of_appetite: Appetite is political in the South again, from the other direction. Mississippi's free pill is defended by its Republican governor as 'cleaning up the counterfeit market' and attacked from the right as 'state-issued hunger suppression'. The backlash coalition of MAHA parents, Unmuted, Bread Alone and fat-acceptance revivalists now has a labelled side effect to point to. It still marches separately: Let Them Grow returned to the Mall in May 2036 with ~85,000, and the Oakland fat-acceptance march was smaller than in 2034.

interior_life.reward_blunting_prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: The class label now states ~6–8% clinically meaningful anhedonia at maintenance doses vs ~3–4% of comparators, ~10% on retatrutide, and ~5% at starting doses. Applied to ~87.8M users, a 3–4 point excess implies roughly 2.5–3.5M Americans whose flattening is attributable to the drug, which is why it is a dinner-table subject. About 38% of current users report a deliberate holiday or self-reduction in the past year. Calm platforms (~2.6M) can no longer sell blunting as the product. They sell 'tuning': lower doses, holiday calendars and mood check-ins.
interior_life.framing: Clinicians, the label and the press now say 'side effect'. Users say 'the flat' and 'taking a weekend'. Platforms say 'dose-tuned'. HR says 'label-directed dose reduction', which is a track code. Unmuted says 'now they admit it'.
interior_life.effect_on_work: Track employers accept clinician-documented dose cuts but penalise unlogged holidays, so workers schedule holidays through telehealth to keep their premium tier. EAPs at trucking and warehousing firms offer Foundayo for AUD. Since 2035, FMCSA medical examiners must ask about anhedonia symptoms but treat them as non-disqualifying. Managers report Friday-skip patterns: sharper Mondays, sicker Mondays. One EEOC charge was dismissed and one is pending.
interior_life.effect_on_art_and_play: 'Holiday' songs, about the weekend you feel things again, charted in country and gospel. The 'off' memoir shelf is now joined by 'tuning' diaries. Comedy moved from 'dry' to 'flat'. Sportsbook handle per account keeps falling, with small spikes on long weekends.
interior_life.effect_on_intimacy: Couples coordinate holidays for anniversaries and sex. Therapists report 'holiday asymmetry': one partner skips to feel the weekend, the other stays on to keep the premium tier. Adult children argue with parents over whether Mom's flatness is the drug or the dementia it is meant to prevent.
interior_life.effect_on_politics: The label gave the backlash a fact. A bipartisan Senate bill to ban adherence-conditioned premiums got a hearing in 2036 but no markup. State politics split oddly: Southern Republican governors fund free pills as anti-counterfeit policy while their primary challengers call it sedation. No turnout effect has been shown.

state.regulatory_posture: Federal regulators stayed permissive on approvals (dementia 60+ extension, Foundayo AUD) and added a class anhedonia label. They are reactive on counterfeits and still punitive on declared imports. States moved for the first time, by spending money rather than regulating.
state.subsidy_or_mandate: Eleven states provide free Wegovy pill (eight for obesity and AUD, three for AUD only) to ~1.1M low-income residents, ~$2.0B a year at TrumpRx prices. No federal subsidy. Medicare became the largest payer through the dementia and AUD labels with no statute changed. The 2027 tri-agency 30% guidance stands.
state.conditioning_or_surveillance: Track data now include dose-reduction codes and holiday logs. State programmes require pharmacy pickup and a quarterly weigh-in at the county health department, and Mississippi shares fill data with its Medicaid agency for de-duplication. CMS's AUD coding audit found ~9% of sampled telehealth AUD diagnoses unsupported, and recoupments began in 2036.
state.workforce_or_military: VA/DoD made incretins first-line for AUD (Jun 2035), and TRICARE and the VA cover them. The Army recruit oral pilot continues. FMCSA added an anhedonia question to driver medical exams.
state.geopolitics_of_supply: The Section 232 100% tariff remains, but India suspended its export-licence checks in Aug 2035 after trade talks failed. Volume now moves through UAE and Mexican transshipment, and the WTO panel on China's complaint has not ruled. Domestic re-filling from smuggled API continues. Novo's oral amycretin shortage is a capacity limit at its US and Danish plants, not a geopolitical one.

events.event: FDA orders class-wide labelling of anhedonia and emotional blunting for incretin drugs, citing rates of 6–8% at maintenance doses against 3–4% in comparators and advising dose reduction; calm platforms drop 'quiet the noise' ads within weeks

Mississippi begins free Wegovy pill provision at county health departments for low-income adults with obesity or alcohol use disorder, paid from general funds and opioid-settlement money at TrumpRx prices; ten more states follow by mid-2036 and about 1.1 million people enrol; the VA/DoD guideline makes incretins first-line for AUD the next month

India suspends its export-licence checks on direct-to-consumer incretin shipments after US trade talks collapse; transshipped vials reach US addresses for $55–120, and in March 2036 FDA and CDC link counterfeit 'oral amycretin' tablets laced with sibutramine to six deaths in nine states

FDA lists oral amycretin in shortage as Novo's oral API capacity falls short; Novo and Lilly tell investors there will be no further US net-price concessions for 2036, ending a decade of annual declines

FDA extends tirzepatide's dementia-risk indication to adults 60 and older with BMI 27 or above, without a cardiovascular requirement but with a fracture-risk limitation; Part D must cover it as a non-weight-loss use, and Medicare incretin users reach about 23 million by December

About 85,000 people return to the Mall for a second 'Let Them Grow' rally, now carrying the anhedonia label; Unmuted's 'Feel Again Week' logs about a million coordinated drug holidays, and a bipartisan bill to ban adherence-conditioned premiums gets a hearing but no vote

open_tensions: Medicare is now the largest incretin payer without Congress ever voting for it. Spending (~$63.8B) rides on labels that are not weight-loss labels, prices stopped falling, and a fracture limitation for women 70+ sits on the same drug sold to them as dementia prevention.
The anhedonia label made drug holidays normal, but conditioned tracks reward continuous logs. The ED networks' Monday vomiting cluster suggests the holidays carry harms nobody has measured.

Eleven mostly Southern states hand out free pills to fight counterfeits, while the cheapest counterfeit tablets ever made are killing people in the same states, and the oral amycretin shortage keeps feeding the counterfeit trade.
Children: Medicaid 6–11 starts keep rising, adult height is still unknown, and 6.1M children now live with a regaining parent, increasingly with a grandparent on the dementia label too.

prose.headline: Medicare Now Pays for More Weight Pills Than Anyone Else, Officially for Your Brain, and the Label Now Admits They Can Leave You Flat
prose.world_in_600_words:
At the end of 2036 almost one American adult in three takes an incretin drug, about eighty-eight million people, and more than four in ten have tried one. The country did not decide this. It happened through labels, shortages and a handful of governors.

The largest change came from a label. In January 2036 the FDA allowed tirzepatide to be prescribed to reduce the risk of dementia in anyone sixty or older carrying extra weight, heart disease or not. Medicare still pays nothing for weight loss alone. That is the statute, and Congress has not touched it. But a dementia pill is not a weight-loss pill, so Part D plans have to cover it. By December about twenty-three million Medicare beneficiaries are on an incretin, and public programmes together are now the largest payer in the market. Part D spends roughly sixty-four billion dollars a year on these drugs. Premiums have gone up twice. In The Villages the early-bird buffets are half empty and the resistance classes are full, because the plans want proof your hips will survive the brain protection. Women over seventy with thin bones are told to take something for their bones first.

The prices stopped falling. For ten years the branded net price slid a few percent a year. Then Medicare demand arrived, Novo could not make enough of its amycretin pill, and the litigation bills came due. The pill went on the shortage list in October 2035, and neither company offered a discount for 2036. The Wegovy starting pill is still $149 through TrumpRx, and six million people still stay on it because it is what they can afford.

The gray market came back. When trade talks with India failed in August 2035, India stopped checking parcels, and vials began reaching American mailboxes through Dubai and Mexico at prices close to their 2032 level. The shortage created a market for fakes. Counterfeit amycretin tablets pressed offshore, some containing an old banned diet drug and a laxative, have been linked to six deaths in nine states. Re-filled vials made another cluster of infections in Alabama.

That is why Mississippi gives the pill away. In May 2035 the state began dispensing the Wegovy pill free at county health departments to poor adults with obesity or drinking problems, paying Novo the same $149 everyone else pays. The governor calls it cleaning up the counterfeit market. Ten states followed, most of them Southern and Republican, and about 1.1 million people collect a bottle with a state seal. Kentucky, West Virginia and Ohio pay only for the alcohol label, with money from the opioid settlements. Bourbon country lost another thousand jobs.

The drug's quietest effect got a label. In March 2035 the FDA required every incretin to warn that six to eight percent of people on full doses lose pleasure in things, against three to four percent of people not on them, and to advise lowering the dose. The calm-plan companies stopped selling the flatness and started selling the tuning. Americans now take drug holidays. They skip the weekend, the wedding or Thanksgiving to feel it, and restart on Monday, sometimes in an emergency room. Employer tracks accept a dose cut signed by a doctor but still count an unlogged skip against the premium tier.

The backlash now has a fact to cite. Let Them Grow brought eighty-five thousand people back to the Mall, and Unmuted's Feel Again Week logged a million coordinated holidays. A Senate bill to ban adherence-conditioned premiums got a hearing and then stalled. Medicaid children aged six to eleven keep starting semaglutide, and nobody yet knows how tall they will be.
prose.a_day_in_the_life:
Lorraine Tate wakes at 5:10 in Greenville, Mississippi, and swallows the pill with four ounces of water, standing at the sink so she won't forget and eat. The bottle has the state seal and her name, and the price line reads $0.00. Thirty minutes. She uses them to iron her daughter's bridesmaid sash.

At the 911 dispatch centre her shift partner, Dewayne, is eating a honey bun. She can smell it and doesn't care. She noticed that sometime last spring, and noticed that she didn't care about the noticing either.

At lunch she calls the county health department. The nurse has the new medication guide open and reads her the questions about pleasure, interest and whether things feel far away. Lorraine answers yes to two of them. The nurse says the label allows a dose cut, but the state programme logs it, and a cut is not the same as stopping. "Don't skip it Saturday on your own," the nurse says. "Folks skip and come back Monday throwing up."

Lorraine says she won't, and she has already decided she will. She wants to cry at the wedding.

After work she drives her mother, seventy-one, to the Walgreens for her tirzepatide. Medicare covers it now as a brain drug, and the bone scan last month was fine. Her mother says she feels "real calm lately," and Lorraine can't tell whether that is the drug or what the drug is supposed to prevent.

In the parking lot her cousin texts a photo of a blister pack labelled amycretin, $60 from a man in Leland, and asks if it looks right.

Lorraine types and deletes three times. Then she sends the CDC link.
